items.title: Dasha 1.10: Patroni auto-discovery, wait analysis and replication slot forecasts for PostgreSQL

items.summary: Dasha 1.10 is an open-source performance dashboard for PostgreSQL fleets featuring Patroni auto-discovery and wait analysis. It affects PostgreSQL database administrators and engineers. Review the release notes to test it on your fleets.

items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
items.snippet: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. They're too good at describing the work The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb. It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high…
items.summary: Simon Willison discusses how AI-generated pull request descriptions from coding agents like Claude Code can be overly verbose. It affects developers reviewing AI-generated code. Read the post to adjust your team's code review workflows.

items.title: Outlook.com Is Quietly Rejecting Email from Domains Without DMARC
